ns2:section.sectionText: This class will explore the contributions of game theory to the field of political science. Although students will learn - or solidify their understanding of - basic game theoretic tools, the emphasis will be on applications of these in contemporary political science research. Students will read academic papers containing formal models and learn to identify the intuition that comes out of them. A wide range of substantive topics will be covered, including comparative electoral politics, protests, environmental cooperation, and civil war. The class is designed to complement Strategic Models I.
ns2:section.sectionNotes: Not intended for students with Freshman class standing.
